summary: Housekeeping and record integrity for the closed snapshot-boundary line. One saved Fact from the earlier five-node attempt (7465f7b9e6cd44e39e8cbf7e2c45c955-knowledge-0) was still stored with a premise now known to be false, so it is revised in place rather than duplicated: the earlier convergence-with-zero-restores result came from a harness whose partition cut only the leader↔majority links, leaving the partner reachable from the majority, so the partner was repaired by the successor during the partition and was already at store 1..4 by the heal. The revision records that only the sealed-partition results remain valid — the retained control receipt beca431464bf44ab9c3354145c21899f showing the TrailingLogs=0 case installing the same snapshot 687–697 times with the follower's applied index pinned at the snapshot index 4 and its last index stuck at 7, versus the TrailingLogs=3 case converging with zero snapshot installs — and names the dependent objects that must not be relied on until re-checked (the two reachability questions and their interpretations, the e4d33475 gap, the standalone correction note b836c3a8-knowledge-0, and the earlier loop question). A new investigation @q-knowledge-lineage carries an 'explained' interpretation with an explicit KnowledgeUse of the revised entry at revision 2, the lineage from superseded run → sealed-partition witness → paired control, and the statement that the narrowing argument resting on the old Fact is withdrawn. No new measurement is claimed; structural validation returned valid=true.
